title: SA/22/2012 of SUNDER SINGH THAPA AND ORS Vs MS BIMLA DEVI AND ORS

paras.text:
SA No. 22 of 2012
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
(Via Video Conferencing)
Mr. Ramji Srivastava, Advocate for
the appellants.
Mr. Arvind Vashistha, Senior
Advocate for the respondents.
This Second Appeal is listed for
orders on the following Applications :
1. MCC No. 640 of 2020
2. CLMA No. 10360 of 2020
3. IA No. 13155 of 2020.
Before answering the rival contentions
raised by the learned counsel for the
parties to the Restoration Application, as
well as to the objection filed to it, this
Court feels it to be inevitable to record the
manner in which the proceedings have
been carried by the parties to the Second
Appeal.
(i) It was, that on 5th July, 1958, Suit
No. 397 of 1958, was instituted for the
grant of a decree of possession and
damages. The said Suit, was initially
decreed on 12th November, 1968.
(ii) Aggrieved as against the said
decree, the First Appeal No. 11 of 1969,
Lal Singh Vs. Ratan Singh was preferred.
The said First Appeal was dismissed on
29th April, 1970.
(iii) Against the First Appellate
Court's judgment dated 29th April, 1970,
the Second Appeal No. 1492 of 1970, was
instituted, before the Allahabad High
Court.
(iv) The said Second Appeal was
allowed by the judgment of 26th July,

1979, and the matter was remanded, and
the proceedings revived back as a
consequence of the judgment of remand
by the Allahabad High Court.
(v) During the pendency of the
proceedings of Appeal on remand, a
Commissioner's report was called upon
and, consequent thereto, the First Appeal
was decided by the Court of Additional
District Judge / FTC 1st, Dehradun, being
Civil Appeal No. 11 of 1969, Lal Singh Vs.
Ratan Singh.
(vi) As against the judgment of 14th
December, 2011, of the First Appellate
Court, the Second Appeal was filed before
the Registry of this Court on 14th March,
2012.
(vii) The diligence, with which, the
appellants, had pursued the Second
Appeal, speaks volumes from the perusal
of the ordersheet, as attempt had been
made to even argue the Second Appeal for
admission, for last 8 years after its
institution.
(viii) On 15th March, 2012, 9th April,
2012, 16th April, 2012 and 19th April,
2012, Registry granted time to the
appellants' Counsel to remove the defects
pointed out by the Registry, but the same
was not removed.
(ix) On 20th April, 2012, the matter
came before the Court and the defect was
reported to have not been removed.
(x) The same situation prevailed as
on 11th May, 2012, the Second Appeal
remained defective.

(xi) Thereafter, the matter was listed
on 23rd April, 2012, 30th April, 2012 and
2nd May, 2012, but the defects were still
not removed.
(xii) On 4th May, 2012, an
adjournment was sought by the counsel
for the appellants, which was repeated on
22nd May, 2012, 8th May, 2013, 2nd July,
2013 and 17th August, 2013 and the
Appeal was never argued till it was lastly
listed on 12th May, 2017, when notices
were issued in the Second Appeal and was
not admitted. Ultimately, when the
Second Appeal was listed on 13th July,
2017, the same was dismissed for want
prosecution, as none had appeared for the
appellants.
(xiii) On the dismissal of the Second
Appeal, the Registry, has sent the
information of dismissal in default, to the
Court below about the fact of an order of
13th July, 2017 on 26th July, 2017, but yet
nothing proceeded at the hands of the
appellants.
(xiv) It was only on 3rd December,
2020, that the appellants had filed the
aforesaid applications as detailed above,
seeking to recall of the order of 13th July,
2017, by invoking the provisions contained
under Order 41 Rule 19 of the C.P.C.
(xv) In the application, thus preferred
by the appellants under Order 41 Rule 19
of the C.P.C., and for the purposes of
condoning the delay, it was only
attributed, to that he could not earlier
acquire the knowledge till the learned
counsel for the appellants conducting the

case before the Court below, Mr. V.K.
Arora, sought an information from the
counsel for the appellants, before the High
Court, on 21st November, 2020.
(xvi) Ultimately, the restoration
application was filed with the delay
condonation application on 29th
November, 2020, with the delay of
1203 days, and the reason for delay,
which has been given in the application is
the lack of information of the order of 13th
July, 2017, and the reason for restoration
as given by the appellants in the
application under Order 41 Rule 19 of the
C.P.C. was that as contained in para 2 of
the restoration application, which is
quoted hereunder :-
"2. That the aforesaid Second Appeal
was listed on 13.7.2017 but inadvertently
the aforesaid appeal could not be
marked in the cause list & therefore the
counsel for the appellants could not
appear when the aforesaid second appeal
was called out, consequently this Hon'ble
Court dismissed the second appeal in
default."
The para 2, where the narration of
fact has been given that due to
inadvertence of the counsel and staff of
his office, its list could not be marked, the
said para has been sworn by the
appellants on the basis of the personal
knowledge. There is no pleading in the
application under Order 41 Rule 19, as to
how the appellants could have got a
personal knowledge of not marking the
cause list by his counsel in the High Court.

The restoration is being seriously
opposed by the learned counsel for the
respondents on the ground that :
(i) It is 62 years old litigation,
which is pending consideration ever since
05.07.1958.
(ii) In view of the judgment rendered
by this Court, in an eventuality, where an
appeal or for that matter any other case, if
is dismissed on account of the mistake of
the counsel or his Office, due to mistake in
not marking the cause list, then the
restoration application is to be supported
with the cause list of the said date in order
to portray that the said case was
mistakingly not marked. All these
materials are lacking to be part of the
records in the restoration application.
Hence, I do not find any merit in the
application under Order 41 Rule 19 of the
C.P.C., in explaining the delay in filing the
restoration application. Consequently, the
Delay Condonation Application is rejected,
and as a consequence thereto, the
restoration too would stand dismissed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
Dated 31.12.2020
Shiv
